question: predict.py writes each prediction row with f.write(...) into a default-buffered text file and never flushes; what reaches disk when the process receives SIGTERM (what SageMaker sends at MaxRuntimeInSeconds)?
writer_script:
import json, sys, time, os
# predict.py's pattern, plus an unbuffered side counter of rows handed to f.write().
fd = os.open(sys.argv[2], os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC)
with open(sys.argv[1], "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for i in range(10**6):
        f.write(json.dumps({"id": f"ext-evl-{i:04d}", "output_text": "{\"units\": []}" + " " * 180, "generated_tokens": 12, "stopped": "eos"}) + "\n")
        os.pwrite(fd, f"{i+1:08d}".encode(), 0)
        time.sleep(0.002)
reading: Finished rows still in the write buffer are lost on SIGTERM (at most one buffer: about 8 KB in the image, i.e. a handful of real prediction rows); lines were never cut. Whether SageMaker uploads /opt/ml/model after a MaxRuntimeInSeconds stop was NOT verified (offline). A per-row flush in predict.py would remove the loss.
